title: Air Fryer Garlic Butter Steak Bites That Beat a $25 Steakhouse Plate
description: Make tender air fryer steak bites at home for $3.50 a serving. Drenched in rich herbed garlic butter, this quick 10-minute dinner beats takeout.
storyHeading: How to Make This for a Fraction of Takeout Cost
story: Paying twenty-two bucks for sirloin tips at a casual diner stopped making sense the day I bought a chuck roast on markdown at Aldi. These air fryer steak bites cost me about three dollars and sixty cents per plate, and honestly, the texture beats a crowded skillet any night. During recipe testing, I learned the hard way that packing too much meat into the basket creates steam instead of a crust—you need to hear that satisfying sizzle. Patting the beef completely dry with a paper towel before tossing it in kosher salt, black pepper, and garlic powder is the entire secret to getting those deeply browned, caramelized edges without overcooking the inside.
ingredients: 1.5 lbs top sirloin or well-marbled chuck roast, cut into uniform 1-inch cubes
1.5 tbsp avocado oil or high-heat cooking oil
instructions: Pat the cubed beef thoroughly dry with paper towels, then toss the pieces in a large bowl with the avocado oil, kosher salt, garlic powder, and black pepper until every piece is evenly coated.
Preheat your air fryer to 400°F for at least 3 minutes so the basket is screaming hot when the meat goes in.

Transfer the seasoned steak bites into the air fryer basket in a single layer, working in two batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding, and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, shaking the basket halfway through.
While the beef cooks, whisk the melted butter, minced garlic, and chopped parsley together in a medium bowl.
Immediately toss the hot cooked steak bites into the garlic herb butter, let them rest for 2 minutes to soak up the juices, and serve warm.
proHack: If you grabbed a cheaper, leaner cut like top round on sale, toss the raw cubes in a tiny pinch of baking soda for 15 minutes before cooking. It alters the pH and keeps the meat remarkably tender in the air fryer.
servingIdea: Serve these over leftover white rice, buttery garlic mashed potatoes, or alongside a crisp wedge salad with ranch dressing to catch all that extra herb butter.
storage: Store leftover steak bites in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a 350°F air fryer for 3 to 4 minutes or toss into a warm skillet for 60 seconds just to warm through without rubbery overcooking.

faqs.question: Can I use frozen steak for air fryer steak bites?
faqs.answer: It is best to start with fully thawed beef. Frozen meat releases too much moisture as it thaws in the basket, which steams the cubes instead of searing that gorgeous crust.

faqs.question: What is the best cut of beef to buy on a budget?
faqs.answer: Top sirloin is usually the best sweet spot for price and tenderness. If budget is tight, chuck roast or bottom sirloin works wonderfully if you cut away any tough connective tissue.
